title: Write planner design: a planning step between reading and coding
summary: Sri's addendum (brief, 2026-10-17) says Athena has no planner and goes straight to coding, which he links to thrashing. I read this as a request for a written design (alternatives, tradeoffs, recommendation) for a planner role between the reader and producer, plus a decision record. The design is not built.

defaults_applied.how: The deliverable is a design with alternatives, not code.
The design cites D01, the thrash-stop text and the BRIEF addendum, and labels numbers as measured or estimated.
One design doc plus a decision entry.
The doc is written for an outside reader.
The criteria check what the design argues and how a verifier would check the plan was followed.
An independent verifier checks cargo test and cargo fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: respond to Sri's observation by designing a planner. Audience: Sri and the Athena maintainers who review designs before building (the 'designed' default).
Per relay note 6A the observation goes to Athena as written, so this job is to analyse it and write the design, not to build a planner.
The 'designed' default requires significant designs to be written with alternatives and reviewed before building, so implementation is a later job.
Whether the planner is an agent or deterministic code is left to the design's recommendation.
question: Should this job only write the planner design, or also implement a planner step in the job lifecycle? I assumed design only, as the designed default asks.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/planner.md states the problem with evidence: D01 in docs/decisions.md has code sequence reader, producer and verifier with no planning step, and the thrash-stop default is prose-only. It cites those sources and Sri's addendum in BRIEF.md.

The design gives at least three alternatives with tradeoffs and a recommendation. Examples: no planner but a stronger reader; a planner agent between reader and producer; a plan section produced inside the reader. It says where the planner sits relative to the planned requirements engineer (addendum 4A), what it outputs, and how a verifier can check the plan was followed.

The design says how the planner would reduce thrashing in a way someone can measure. It names a signal, such as repeated failures of the same item or rejected jobs per request, and labels any numbers as estimates or measured.

docs/decisions.md has a new decision entry (Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost, Provenance) that matches the design and notes its relation to D01's 'a planner could later sit above it' remark.
Only docs change. No Rust source, athena.toml, defaults.toml, or workflow files are modified, and no planner is implemented. The design lists that as out of scope.
Run `cargo test` and `cargo fmt --check` from the repository root. Both pass, so any doc-consistency tests (for example on decision numbering or links) still hold.

out_of_scope: Implementing the planner or changing the job lifecycle in Rust
Building the requirements engineer (4A) or the shared vocabulary (5A)
Changing BRIEF.md or the Olympus rebrand
departures: The request is ambiguous between a design and an implementation, which lowers acceptance a little. Design-only work is cheaper to verify.
